ComputeConfig.description:
The size and lifetime of the environment. Every field is optional. An
omitted field takes the platform default (2 vCPUs, 4096 MiB, a 4h timeout,
10m idle). A value outside the platform bounds fails validation.

`memory` accepts a string such as `8GB` or an object such as `{gb: 8}`.
`timeout` and `idle` accept a duration string such as `30m`, `8h`, or
`1h30m`.

`timeout` is the longest one message's work may run before it is stopped,
1m to 22h, default 4h. The message ends `stopped` with reason `timeout`.

`idle` is how long the environment stays awake after the agent finishes
with no message waiting, 10s to 1h, default 10m. Then it pauses, and the
next message resumes it. Only an interactive session pauses. A session
that runs once ends when its message ends.
ComputeConfig.title: ComputeConfig

EnvironmentConfig.description:
Everything about the environment the agent runs in: which
`repositories` are cloned into it, which environment `variables` it gets,
its `compute` sizing, lifecycle `hooks`, and the `mcp` servers every
session in it gets, next to the session's own `mcp`.
What the agent may *do* from that environment, `permissions:`, sits on
the session config, not here.

Each `variables` entry names a variable to inject; with an inline `value` it
is hardcoded, without one it is resolved from the account's secrets
store. Only the named variables reach this agent; the rest of the account's
stored variables never do. This is how a config brings in the config and
credentials a custom CLI needs.
EnvironmentConfig.title: EnvironmentConfig

EnvironmentHooks.description:
Environment lifecycle scripts, in order: build_base, after_checkout,
before_start, validate. The first two produce reusable snapshots;
before_start runs before an agent starts or resumes its session, and
validate runs last to check that the environment has what the agent needs.
Scripts run as the environment's user in the workspace directory
`/sandbox`. A nonzero exit fails the session.

Legacy post_start/post_clone scripts remain supported for existing configs;
both run after workspace preparation, before the agent starts or resumes.
They cannot be combined with the new lifecycle fields.

after_checkout.description: Prepare the requested source revision after Ellipsis checks out all repositories, before saving the prepared environment. Skipped when that prepared environment is reused.
after_checkout.title: After Checkout

before_start.description: Run before the agent starts or resumes a session, after the environment is ready. This hook is not cached and adds to session startup time.
before_start.title: Before Start

build_base.description: Build a reusable environment before full checkout. Cached by declared inputs, script, toolchain, resources, and build configuration. A string is shorthand for run with all repositories as inputs.
build_base.title: Build Base

post_clone.description: Legacy session startup script. Use before_start for session setup or after_checkout for cached source preparation.
post_clone.title: Post Clone

post_start.description: Legacy session startup script. Use before_start in new configurations.
post_start.title: Post Start

validate.description: Check that the environment works, for example that required tools are on PATH. Runs last, after before_start, each time a session starts or resumes and each time the environment is built after a change. A nonzero exit fails the session or the build. Not cached.
validate.title: Validate

EnvironmentHooks.title: EnvironmentHooks

EnvironmentSource.description:

EnvironmentVariable.description:
One environment variable injected into the session's environment.

`value`, when set, is a literal injected as-is — use it for non-secret
config (LOG_LEVEL, an API base URL). When `value` is omitted the value is
resolved at run time from the account's secrets store (dashboard
/ `PUT /v1/secrets`) by `name`, so a secret can be injected without
ever putting it in the config file. Either way the variable only reaches
agents that name it.
EnvironmentVariable.title: EnvironmentVariable

anyOf.description:
One include-minus-exclude set of GitHub accounts: an account matches iff
it is in `include` (`true` = all, a list = exactly those, `false`/`[]` =
none) AND not in `exclude`. A bare bool or list is shorthand for `include`,
so `users: true` and `users: [priya-shah]` both parse.
anyOf.title: GithubAccountFilter

GithubAccountSelector.description:
A selector of GitHub accounts — the `for:` audience gate on react
surfaces, classified on the stable entity author (the pusher for `push`,
the PR author for a pull request). `users` selects human
accounts, `bots` selects bot accounts; each is a `GithubAccountFilter`
(include minus exclude, with bare bool/list shorthand).

`teams` narrows further to members of any of the listed GitHub teams of
the installation's organization, by slug (`platform` for
`@org/platform`). It applies on top of `users`: the author must pass the
users filter AND belong to a listed team. A bot is never a team member,
so a selector with `teams` never admits one. Membership is resolved live
at match time, and the config sync refuses a team that does not exist
when the file is accepted.
GithubAccountSelector.title: GithubAccountSelector

GithubAccountSnippet.description:

using this snippet instead of the full GithubAccount model. One example,
is when the API returns a pull request.

This is the least amount of info we need to represent a GitHub account.
GithubAccountSnippet.title: GithubAccountSnippet

ReactLinearIssue.description:
A Linear issue being created (`opened`), changed (`updated`), or
delegated to Ellipsis (`delegated`). An
`updated` event fires only when every field under `changed` changed in
one edit. `team`, `state`, `labels`, `project`, `assignee`, and
`priority` filter on the issue as it is after the event. `state` matches
a status name or a status type. `for` is the person who created,
changed, or delegated the issue. A delegation an agent or an automation
made counts as a bot's.
ReactLinearIssue.title: ReactLinearIssue

ReactRelease.description:
A GitHub release being published — a release or prerelease published
directly, or a draft published later. `tag` narrows to the release tags
that match (exact, or a prefix ending in `*`, so `v*`); `prerelease`
selects prereleases or full releases, like `draft` on pull requests. The
`for:` audience is the release's author, which for a release cut by CI is
a bot and needs `bots` to opt in.
ReactRelease.title: ReactRelease

ReactStatus.description: A commit status changing state, from CI that posts statuses instead of checks. `names` matches status contexts exactly or by a prefix ending in `*`. `branch` matches when any branch GitHub lists for the commit matches. `for` works as on `check_run`. Needs the Commit statuses permission.
ReactStatus.title: ReactStatus

ReactTrigger.description:
An event trigger: exactly one surface block names the events to match.

`enabled: false` pauses the trigger and keeps its definition: events stop
matching while the agent stays live for on-demand starts and open
sessions keep taking follow-ups (`ellipsis.enabled: false` pauses the
whole file instead).
ReactTrigger.title: ReactTrigger

ReactWorkflowRun.description: A GitHub Actions workflow run changing state. `names` matches workflow names exactly or by a prefix ending in `*`. `branch` is the branch the run is for. `for` works as on `check_run`. Needs the Actions permission.
ReactWorkflowRun.title: ReactWorkflowRun

ReleaseAction.description:
What happened to a GitHub release. `published` is the one moment a
release becomes visible: a release or prerelease published directly, or a
draft published later. Edits, deletions, and unpublishes never fire.
ReleaseAction.title: ReleaseAction

anyOf.description:
The watch scope of a trigger, by repository name (owner defaults to the
account). Include minus exclude: `include: []` (the default) covers every
repository of the installation, so `exclude`-only means "all except these"
and keeps covering repositories added to the org later. A bare list is
shorthand for `include`.
anyOf.title: RepositoryFilter

SandboxCacheTier.description: Which image-cache tier a sandbox creation took.

Session.description:
An agent session: one conversation with an agent. Returned by
`GET /v1/sessions/{id}` and carried by the session stream's
`session` frames; REST and stream never disagree about what a
session looks like.

agent.description: The agent the session was started from, or null for a raw session started with POST /v1/sessions.

archived.description: When and by whom the session was archived, or null when it isn't. A session is archived when it closes, after the account's archive_inactive_sessions_days without a message, or by PUT /v1/sessions/{id}. An archived session takes no messages, and a reply on the Slack thread, pull request, issue, or Linear issue it answers starts a new session.

budget.description: The spend budget enforced for this session.

claude_code.description: Claude Code input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code, codex, or gemini.

codex.description: Codex input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code, codex, or gemini.

content_deleted_at.description: When session log retention deleted the session's records, messages, and prompt, or null. The session's status, cost, tokens, and summary stay.
content_deleted_at.title: Content Deleted At

conversation.description: Whether the session can take more messages, and whether an agent is warm to answer one.

cost.description: What the session has cost so far.

environment.description: The full environment configuration frozen when the session was created, with the saved environment's id and how it was chosen.

error.description: Why the last message failed, was stopped, or was cancelled; null otherwise.

event.description: The webhook that started the session, as the integration sent it. Null for api, cli, web, and cron starts.

gemini.description: Gemini CLI input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code, codex, or gemini.

mcp.description: Every MCP server the session has: the servers its environment lists, its own, and the Slack or Linear server of a session started from Slack or Linear.
mcp.title: Mcp

metadata.description: Labels and annotations set when the session started.

output.description: The session's structured output: the `json_schema` the agent must satisfy and, once the agent has submitted it, the `result`.

parent.description: The predecessor session this session continues; null when there is none.

permissions.description: What the session may touch, per minted credential.

review.description: The code review this session ran for; null unless the source is `code_review`.

scm.description: What the session did in source control, by provider. Per repository: the commit and branch it sits on, its commits, each uncommitted file with its line counts and diff, and the pull requests it opened.

source.description: Where the session came from (e.g. react, web, api, cli, mention, cron).

status.description: Where the session is. A message you sent is answered once the status is `idle` or `closed`; its `message_ended` record in GET /v1/sessions/{id}/records says how.

summary.description: The latest live summary of the session's progress while it runs, and when it was generated.

tokens.description: The tokens the session has used so far.

updated_at.description: When the session was last updated.
updated_at.title: Updated At

url.description: The session's page in the dashboard.
url.title: Url

user.description: The person who started this session; null for scheduled sessions and API keys with no creator.

wait_ms.description: Milliseconds from when the session was created to when it started, including any time it waited because your account already had its limit of sessions alive. Null until the session starts, and for sessions created before this field was added.
wait_ms.title: Wait Ms

Session.title: Session

SessionArchived.description: When the session was archived and the user who archived it.

by.description: The user who archived the session. Null when no user did.

deletes_at.description: When the session's records and messages are deleted, from the account's current session log retention. It moves when the retention changes. Null when they're already deleted.
deletes_at.title: Deletes At

SessionArchived.title: SessionArchived

SessionBudget.description:
The spend budget actually enforced for this session, and which layer of
the cascade set it.

limit.description: The most this session may spend, in millicents, after resolving defaults and ceilings.
limit.title: Limit

source.description: Where the limit came from. `config` is the agent's config, `account` is the account's default, and `system` is the platform's maximum, which caps the other two.

SessionBudget.title: SessionBudget

SessionConfig.description:
What one session runs on: its selected harness, where it runs, what it
may touch, its skills, its MCP servers, its exit contract, and its spend
cap. An agent
carries one under `session:`, and `POST /v1/sessions` is this shape
flattened onto the request body, plus the run settings.

claude_code.description: Claude Code input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code, codex, or gemini.

codex.description: Codex input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code, codex, or gemini.

gemini.description: Gemini CLI input and native options. Set exactly one of claude_code, codex, or gemini.

metadata.description: Labels and annotations stored on every session.

SessionConfig.title: SessionConfig

SessionConversation.description:
Whether the session can take more messages, and how quickly it would
answer one.

interactive.description: Whether the session stays open after its first message is answered.
interactive.title: Interactive

prompting.description: The session's policy for direct messages. Caller authorization and message validation are checked separately.

warm.description: Whether an agent is ready to answer the next message right away. When false, the next message first prepares an environment, which takes longer. A hint only; clients need no logic on it.
warm.title: Warm

SessionConversation.title: SessionConversation

SessionConversationConfig.description: Conversation settings for a session, set on a saved agent or sent when starting a session or running an agent.

interactive.description: Whether the session stays open after its first message is answered. Defaults to true; false runs once and requires a prompt. Requires the model's interactive capability when true. Direct message acceptance is reported separately in conversation.prompting.
interactive.title: Interactive

SessionConversationConfig.title: SessionConversationConfig

SessionEnvironment.description:
The environment configuration frozen at session creation, enriched with
the saved environment's identity and how it was chosen.

id.description: Identifier of the saved environment the session's config resolved. Null for an inline environment block or the built-in basic environment.
id.title: Id

source.description: How the environment was chosen (request, agent, platform_default; repo_default and account_default on sessions from before those ladders were removed). An inline request uses request; an inline environment declared in session configuration has no source.

SessionEnvironment.title: SessionEnvironment

SessionError.description:
Why the last message failed, was stopped, or was cancelled. Cleared
when the next message starts.
SessionError.title: SessionError

SessionGit.description:
Every repo the session touched. Small enough to ride on `sessions`
and be returned by every session read.
SessionGit.title: SessionGit

SessionGitCommit.description:
One commit the session created in this repo (everything past the
provisioning checkout's sha), captured from the environment rather than the
transcript so it stays correct through amends, rebases, and commits made by
scripts. The repo is the parent object, so it is not repeated here.
SessionGitCommit.title: SessionGitCommit

SessionGitFile.description:
One file's uncommitted change, as `git diff HEAD --numstat` reports it
(with intent-to-add, so a brand-new file still counts).

patch.description: The file's unified diff, `diff --git` header included, exactly as git emitted it. Null when the session's diff passed 100 KB and this file was left out.
patch.title: Patch

SessionGitFile.title: SessionGitFile

SessionGitPr.description:
A pull request the session opened in this repo, written the moment the
creating tool call's result lands (see extract_session_prs.PrCreateWatcher).
Live PR state (open/merged/closed) is not stored — it lives on gh_prs,
joined via `gh_pr_id` (GET /frontend/agents/sessions/{id}/git). The repo is
the parent object, so it is not repeated here.

pull_request.description: The pull request as GitHub last reported it. Null until Ellipsis has read it from GitHub.

SessionGitPr.title: SessionGitPr

SessionGitRepo.description:
One checkout in the session's environment and everything the session did
to it, split by whether it survived the environment.
SessionGitRepo.title: SessionGitRepo

SessionOutput.description:
Structured output on the wire: the contract and, when the agent has
submitted one, the payload. `result` is None while the session runs and
when the agent submitted nothing; it is the agent's own JSON, in the
shape of `json_schema`.

json_schema.description: JSON Schema the agent's result must satisfy.
json_schema.title: Json Schema

result.description: The payload the agent submitted, or null until it submits one.
result.title: Result

SessionOutput.title: SessionOutput

SessionParent.description: The predecessor session this session continues.

id.description: Identifier of the predecessor session this session continues.
id.title: Id

SessionParent.title: SessionParent

SessionPrompting.description:
The prompt-affordance projection. `enabled` answers "would a send work",
and when it wouldn't, `blocked_reason` + `detail` say why.

`surface_name` is set only for MENTION_SURFACE, naming where to reply.
SessionPrompting.title: SessionPrompting

SessionReview.description: The code review a reviewer session ran for.
SessionReview.title: SessionReview

SessionScm.description: What the session did in source control, by provider.

github.description: Each GitHub repository in the session's environment and what the session did to it. Null if nothing was ever captured.

SessionScm.title: SessionScm

SessionSource.description:
Where a session came from: the credential that started it (web app,
API key, CLI) or the trigger that fired (react, mention, cron, code
review). Never taken from a request body.
SessionSource.title: SessionSource

SessionStatus.description:
Where the session is. `queued` while a message waits for a worker,
`preparing` while its environment is set up, `running` while the agent
works, `idle` when every message has been answered and the session can
take another, and `closed` when it can take no more. `closed` is
permanent.
SessionStatus.title: SessionStatus

SessionSummary.description:
A live one-line summary of what the session is doing, refreshed
every few steps while it runs.

created_at.description: When this summary line was generated. Null on summaries written before generation time was tracked.
created_at.title: Created At

description.description: One-line description of what the session is doing.
description.title: Description

source.description: Where this summary came from. `prompt` is the first line of the prompt the session started with, `generated` is written by Ellipsis as the session runs, and `user` was set by a person and is never replaced by a generated one.

SessionSummary.title: SessionSummary

SessionSummarySource.description: Where a session's summary came from.
SessionSummarySource.title: SessionSummarySource

SettingsRef.description:

SettingsRef.title: SettingsRef

SkillRef.description:
